- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion or hidden support.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days of falling prices, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward bias if price has been above 30-day moving average for >5 days.
